summary: Product Owner with nearly 10 years of product management experience spanning B2B recruitment and consumer subscription apps, with experience in account security, messaging, pricing, payments and localization. Manage direct reports and align stakeholder priorities, translating business requirements into specifications and coordinating cross-team delivery. Use AI agents (Claude Code, Antigravity) for specification writing and data analysis within a human-in-the-loop workflow, retaining ownership of final product decisions.
skills: Requirements & Validation: Requirements Analysis, PRD, User Story, Use Case, Process & Sequence Diagrams, Prototyping, UAT
Design & Agentic AI Tools: Axure RP, Figma, Claude Code, Antigravity
Delivery & Commercial Methods: Kanban, Stakeholder Alignment, Pricing Experiments, Payment Integration Planning
personal_statement: Across dating and subscription apps, an influencer-matching platform and an employer recruitment system, I keep returning to two questions: can users achieve what they came for, and does the product help the company keep running? I like shaping products from ideas that have not yet taken form, and I want teams to understand the judgment behind a plan, not only the list of features.

KOOL, an influencer-matching platform, confirmed the work I enjoy most: starting from what merchants and influencers each need, and turning scattered ideas into an experience that works for both sides. Invitations, applications and messaging are more than a feature list; one side's actions have to connect to the other side's needs.

When JustDating and then Juicy were removed from the App Store, I faced the pressure of carrying existing users and revenue forward. Shipping the product was not enough; I also had to coordinate App Store communication and marketing traffic to keep the service running. Those two experiences taught me to plan with the dependencies between teams in view, so that launch and traffic routing are part of the product plan.

I joined 1111 to take part in overhauling a whole recruitment system. When I took over the employer-side recruitment system overhaul in late 2024, I first established what the new design could rely on: account permissions and business-model rules had no documentation, so I derived them from actual operation and checked them with engineering, operations and audit. Once the relationship between existing data and operations was clear, I could plan the login and company-data changes so that the new design connected to the service still running.

Moving from influencer matching to employer recruitment, I extended the question of how two sides find each other to how members of the same organization work together. The shared recruitment feature had to consider accounts, job posts and resumes together, so that large employers could recruit by department or branch. I anticipate exceptions in advance so users spend less time stopping to figure things out.

Today I use AI agents such as Antigravity and Claude Code for specifications and data analysis: I define the problem, rules and verification requirements, then guide the AI to check and add information with a confidence level, and people judge the results and exceptions. When I teach colleagues to work with AI, I start from where they are stuck and show them how to guide the AI and check its output, so they can judge for themselves and we discuss only the few exceptions. What I want to pass on is a way of working: let the tool help, and keep human judgment.

Next, I want to combine my experience in subscriptions, pricing and enterprise workflows to take part in requirement trade-offs under a business direction, staying involved from planning through launch. I also care whether a product, after delivery, actually improves the user experience and brings business value.

description_bullets: Product Owner of an employer-side recruitment system serving about 60,000 active paying employers (2026 Q3), covering job posting, applicant management and candidate outreach. Manage two product planners as direct reports and coordinate engineering, design, sales and customer service.

In March–April 2026, after more than ten employer recruitment accounts were hijacked, coordinated the response with engineering and customer service. Designed and launched new-device OTP login verification (MFA) and an account-unlock flow. Through October 2026, customer service received no reports of similar account-takeover incidents.

Planned a unified messaging flow for employers and job seekers to address 199 client requests accumulated since 2021. It consolidates two overlapping tools that had split interview invitations across separate channels, and is now in development.

To lower the barrier to job posting and improve candidate matching, led the launch of AI-generated job descriptions (2024/10) and AI talent recommendations (2025/11), and guided direct reports in launching company-profile generation (2026/06). Defined labor-law compliance acceptance criteria and required employer confirmation of generated content before publishing. Refined recommendation rules using employers' actual selections and feedback.

Led requirements analysis and specification planning to ship about 70 major features by 2026 Q3, even as ongoing service iterations and a full system overhaul competed for the same engineering resources. Aligned stakeholders and secured sales buy-in before delivery.

Reverse-engineered undocumented account permissions and business rules for the employer-side recruitment system overhaul; 743 of 840 related client requests (88%) were resolved during the overhaul. Used hands-on testing and internal interviews, then coordinated phased replacement of legacy functions while keeping the existing back office, database and live service running.

In response to 55 client requests since 2020/12, planned a shared recruitment feature allowing employers to manage hiring by department or branch. Defined access rules across accounts, job posts and resumes, along with legacy data migration rules, extending the original company-wide or individual-account data access.

Raised the 30-day case closure rate for enterprise clients' product issues and suggestions from 52% to 79% (2024/11–2025/10 vs. 2025/11–2026/09/20; cases submitted at least 30 days earlier). To support paying employers' satisfaction and renewals, prioritized client cases, handled key cases directly and delegated others to direct reports, building the product team's delivery credibility with sales.

Audited and consolidated 15 shared category code tables (job roles, certifications, skills and benefits) starting 2026/04 by reviewing the underlying data fields used in job posting, resume creation, search filtering and matching across the platform. Addressed fragmentation that had built up as the business expanded. Used an AI agent to assist in structuring field-level mappings and organizing handoff records, and guided colleagues in using AI to map hundreds of job categories.

description_bullets: Managed JustDating, the company's flagship and highest-grossing subscription dating app. According to public company information, JustDating long held the No. 1 position on Taiwan's dating app revenue chart. Also managed Peach, a subscription content app, and KOOL, an influencer-matching platform. Planned user flows, subscriptions and payment mechanisms with engineering, design, marketing and overseas payment teams, and held partnership discussions with a European payment provider in English over video calls.

Led the design of a three-phase Malaysia iOS pricing experiment (original price, then discounted price, then original price; 2021/05–08, 21 days each), with Android held at an unchanged price as the control group. In the discount phase, iOS revenue excluding renewals rose 5% versus the original-price phase, while Android fell 18%. After the original price was restored, iOS revenue excluding renewals fell 65% versus the original-price phase. The company owner adopted the lower price based on the experiment results.

Raised web payments' share of revenue for the subscription content app Peach from 24% to over 80% (2020/11–2021/09) by planning the shift from in-app purchases to web payments and coordinating integration with a payment provider in Taiwan.

With no direct competitor to benchmark against, planned KOOL from zero to one, starting with interviews with merchants' marketing teams about how they found influencers on Instagram. Adapted listing and matching mechanics from Airbnb and dating apps, and mapped invitation, application and messaging flows in Miro. After the project kicked off in 2018/05, coordinated product, design and engineering to launch across iOS, Android and web. The platform accumulated about 16,000 influencer profiles and over 80,000 campaign applications in six months. Led the monetization rollout covering VIP subscriptions, a points paywall and featured exposure.

When the App Store removed JustDating, led the launch of Juicy, a replacement app on the same backend, to retain existing users and revenue. After Juicy was removed, led JustDating's relaunch. Across both launches and their accompanying marketing campaigns directing users to the apps, male daily active users (DAU) rose from about 3,200 to 12,500 over 6 weeks for Juicy (2020/01–02) and from about 1,500 to 12,000 over 12 weeks for JustDating (2020/04–06), reflecting overall product performance.

description_bullets: Maintained and improved SweetRing, a dating app operating across 7 markets (US, Mexico, Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Japan, Korea), including its question-and-answer feature. Also took part in localization and payment planning.

Expanded payment options in Indonesia and Thailand by bringing in CodaPay, a Southeast Asian payment provider, and opening 8 payment channels (carrier billing, ATM, e-wallets, convenience stores, bank transfer). Compared fees and settlement terms, estimated net revenue, proposed 7-, 30- and 90-day subscription plans, and coordinated delivery of the Android top-up page.

Coordinated localization across the 7 markets, translating the app's Chinese UI text into English as the shared baseline. Worked with up to about 10 foreign interns in English-only meetings to translate that baseline into local languages and run local fan pages.
